text:
alex: heads-up — proposing a small-but-invasive schema change for how we store per-tenant dashboard aggregates. goal: remove the heavy route-level JSON blob and normalize to a per-tenant metrics_facts table so dashboard queries stop scanning huge jsonb columns and p99 queries improve. thoughts?

maria: do you have a sketch of the new write/read path? curious about back-compat with existing console cards.

alex: yep — rough plan:
- keep ingest API unchanged (we’ll continue to write to events_raw).
- add tenant_metrics_facts(tenant_id, metric_day, metric_key, value, version) as the new normalized store.
- a small background worker will materialize writes from events_raw -> facts (canary mode) and maintain a shadow aggregated column on routes table for any live fallback.

sam: how do we intend to handle tenant-scoped quotas/ingest throttles? metric_key cardinality could explode if we just denormalize naively.

alex: agree — we’ll limit metric_key namespace to the 12 keys used by console cards (route_p95, route_error_rate, token_cost, etc). Any non-supported key lands in metrics_aux JSON blob. Also TTL compaction at 90d for raw events.

kevin: example migration SQL? want to run perf estimate on staging.

alex: sure — early snippet for the facts table:

```sql
CREATE TABLE tenant_metrics_facts (
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
  metric_day date NOT NULL,
  metric_key text NOT NULL,
  value double precision NOT NULL,
  version integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, metric_day, metric_key)
);

-- lightweight index for dashboard range scans
CREATE INDEX ON tenant_metrics_facts (metric_day, metric_key);
```

jen: are we planning dual-write for the console API reads? dashboards still query the old route_metrics view right now.

alex: yes — plan is a staged coexistence:
1) shadow write facts from ingest worker (no read traffic).
2) run a nightly backfill to populate historical days for high-volume tenants.
3) provide a read adapter that implements the existing route_metrics view by querying facts + metric_aux JSON for missing keys. This read adapter will be behind a feature flag route:console_metrics_v2.

nora: what are the rollback considerations? if the adapter has a bug we can't break dashboards.

alex: feature-flagged reads + fallback: adapter will run a quick-row-check against sample keys; if mismatch > 0.5% for any tenant in the canary cohort, we auto-fallback to the old view for that tenant. migration-bot will post alerts.

migration-bot: migration-check scheduled: shadow pipeline start at 2025-08-12T02:00Z; canary cohort size 5% of active tenants; metric mismatch threshold 0.5%.

sam: perf concerns: will the facts table introduce hotspots when many tenants request the same metric_day? we may need to shard by tenant_id hash to keep writes distributed.

alex: good call — initial PK keeps tenant first to allow efficient single-tenant reads. for write scale we can partition by metric_day + tenant_id MOD N if we see contention. also batching writes in the worker.

kevin: query rewrite for dashboard — can you paste the new view SQL? I'll run explain on staging.

alex: simplified view (pseudo):

```sql
CREATE VIEW route_metrics AS
SELECT r.route_id, f.metric_day, f.metric_key, f.value
FROM routes r
LEFT JOIN tenant_metrics_facts f ON f.tenant_id = r.tenant_id AND f.metric_key IN ('route_p95','route_error_rate')
WHERE f.metric_day >= current_date - interval '7 days';
```

jen: need to check BI/analytics downstream ETL that expects the old JSON shape. we should catalog consumers and add compatibility mappings.

nora: we should also add a small telemetry event emitted by the read adapter when fallback occurs so console SRE can view per-tenant flip rate.

alex: yep telemetry events: console.read.adapter.fallback with tags tenant_id, reason, mismatch_rate. add to dashboard for migration-runbook.

sam: testing checklist suggestion:
- unit tests for worker aggregation logic
- integration test: ingest -> shadow facts -> view parity test across 1000 synthetic tenants
- smoke canary: 5% tenants for 48h with mismatch monitor
- perf test: 1h synthetic high-write burst to check hotspots

kevin: can we avoid a huge backfill by making the view combine recent days from facts (if present) and fallback to events_raw aggregation for older days? that reduces initial backfill scope.

alex: yes, view will prefer facts for any day present and compute from events_raw otherwise. plan to backfill last 90 days only for top 200 tenants to start.

jen: legal asked about data retention and KMS for backups — if we create the facts table we must ensure any snapshotting or replication respects tenant data retention policies. cc @security later.

alex: noted. I'll add a retention metadata column and hook into the snapshot exclusion list during PG base backups.

nora: can we add a lightweight synthetic metric to track cost-savings estimate? e.g., average query tokens / p99 latency pre/post. helps product tell the story.

alex: agreed — add console.migration.estimated_cost_delta and console.migration.latency_p99. we'll populate after canary.

maria: timeline?

alex: proposed timeline:
- next week: schema + worker in staging (no reads)
- week after: start shadow pipeline and small canary (5%)
- +2 weeks: extend canary to 20% and run perf test
- +1 month: staged backfill of top tenants + flip feature flag for more tenants if stable

sam: +1 on the plan. make sure we add a customer-facing note if dashboards may show small variance during migration window.

alex: will draft a console status page blurb and ping support. thanks everyone — I'll open a PR with the worker + view adapter and link it here. :thumbsup:
